title: Brazil's TCU captures R$426 million through its ALICE tender-analysis robot in 2021
summary: TCU says its ALICE tender-analysis robot captured R$426m in 2021 (R$194m in 2020); specific cases reported only via press
account: The Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) operates ALICE, a text-mining robot. It reads federal tender notices and electronic-auction records daily and sends auditors a list of possible irregularities. Trade press in 2017 and 2018 expanded the name as “Análise de Licitações e Editais”. The TCU's own July 2020 release calls it the “Sistema de Análise de Licitações e Contratos (Alice)”. In its 4 March 2022 statement on 2021 control benefits, the TCU reported the value captured through Alice. It was R$426 million in 2021 against R$194 million in 2020. Only the year is given, so 1 January 2021 is used. Trade press in September 2017 quoted TCU auditor Valéria Nakano that Alice found two DNIT notices worth R$39 million. They were for maintaining BR-153 stretches already under concession, blocked by an acórdão within two months. That acórdão could not be obtained, so the example is unverified.
purpose: Daily automated screening of federal procurement notices to direct external-control auditors to likely irregularities
system: ALICE, expanded as 'Análise de Licitações e Editais' in 2017 and 2018 press reports and named 'Sistema de Análise de Licitações e Contratos (Alice)' in the TCU's July 2020 release, with companion tools SOFIA and MONICA; evolved into ALICE 360 by 2026
developer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), in-house
deployer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU); also shared with DNIT and the Ministry of Infrastructure under a 2020 agreement
domain: Public administration: external audit and procurement control

ratings.reason: Aggregate program figure with no discrete attributable event.
The R$426 million is an annual total of control benefits credited to the Alice system, not a single verified event.
Aggregate. The TCU's own benefit-measurement methodology, not an independent evaluation.

ai_role.statement: The TCU attributes the 2021 figure to control actions supported by Alice under its benefit-measurement method. It says “o segundo de fato reflete o benefício calculado, que resultou da ação de controle e foi medido”. No independent evaluation or counterfactual was found. The 2017 DNIT/BR-153 example rests on a trade-press interview with a TCU auditor. The TCU acórdão was not available. Developer and deployer are the same public body.

fields.account: The Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) operates ALICE, a text-mining robot. It reads federal tender notices and electronic-auction records daily and sends auditors a list of possible irregularities. Trade press in 2017 and 2018 expanded the name as “Análise de Licitações e Editais”. The TCU's own July 2020 release calls it the “Sistema de Análise de Licitações e Contratos (Alice)”. In its 4 March 2022 statement on 2021 control benefits, the TCU reported the value captured through Alice. It was R$426 million in 2021 against R$194 million in 2020. Only the year is given, so 1 January 2021 is used. Trade press in September 2017 quoted TCU auditor Valéria Nakano that Alice found two DNIT notices worth R$39 million. They were for maintaining BR-153 stretches already under concession, blocked by an acórdão within two months. That acórdão could not be obtained, so the example is unverified.

fields.summary: TCU says its ALICE tender-analysis robot captured R$426m in 2021 (R$194m in 2020); specific cases reported only via press
fields.account: The Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) operates ALICE, a text-mining robot. It reads federal tender notices and electronic-auction records daily and sends auditors a list of possible irregularities. Trade press in 2017 and 2018 expanded the name as “Análise de Licitações e Editais”. The TCU's own July 2020 release calls it the “Sistema de Análise de Licitações e Contratos (Alice)”. In its 4 March 2022 statement on 2021 control benefits, the TCU reported the value captured through Alice. It was R$426 million in 2021 against R$194 million in 2020. Only the year is given, so 1 January 2021 is used. Trade press in September 2017 quoted TCU auditor Valéria Nakano that Alice found two DNIT notices worth R$39 million. They were for maintaining BR-153 stretches already under concession, blocked by an acórdão within two months. That acórdão could not be obtained, so the example is unverified.
